purpose: Independent behavioral confirmation of the complete V2-M1 through V2-M3 authorization chain on fresh data

amendment_record.reason: The V4 (reacquisition_window) and V5 (identity_switch_penalty_weight) amendments each addressed one precise, independently-diagnosed friction in the V2-I1 system-integration probe (docs/experiments/V2_I1_INTEGRATION_REPORT.md), but a track that is mis-associated even once has its theta/autonomous_velocity updated from the wrong displacement on that very step, and every prediction generated afterward is built on this now-corrupted state - no amount of tuning the association cost (V5) prevents 100% of bad associations, and neither amendment gave a track any way to recover once one occurred. Separately, cheap integration-layer fixes (a revocable self-lock, and pruning a different, independent stale-entity list in the M4-side OccupancyMemory) measurably improved V2-I1's self_f1 and distractor_hidden_probability but left identity_consistency completely unchanged across all three interventions - isolating it as a problem specifically in this locked component's own track-state continuity, unfixable from the integration layer or the M4-side mechanism. This amendment adds a `drift_reset_after` constructor parameter (default None, a hard no-op: the reset branch is gated on `self.drift_reset_after is not None`, so it is skipped entirely, not just numerically inert, for every existing caller). When enabled, an unmatched track that has gone unseen for more than `drift_reset_after` steps AND whose raw control_evidence has gone negative (not `probability`: in a world where control_evidence rarely climbs high even for a genuinely correct track, probability can sit low regardless of whether a track is actually corrupted, so it cannot discriminate a real mis-association from ordinary weak-but-real evidence; going negative is a stronger, rarer signal that recent residuals were worse than the autonomous-only baseline) - i.e. one that reacquisition_window's own accounting would soon give up on anyway, not a confident track merely riding out a normal occlusion - has its theta, covariance, and autonomous_velocity wiped back to the same blank values `_new_track` uses, and its control_evidence/probability reset to a neutral prior. Position, last_seen, and index are left untouched: this does not create a new identity, it lets a corrupted one re-learn cleanly under the same index instead of coasting on a poisoned estimate until pruning. Verified empirically, not just argued: development-split results for V2-M2 (all three association modes, plus the legacy path) and V2-M3 (plus its no-causal-likelihood ablation) were captured before this change and re-run after it with the new code's default parameter; every field is byte-for-byte identical except cpu_wall_seconds (a timing measurement, not a behavioral output). No existing caller (v2_m2.py, v2_m3_hypotheses.py, v2_m1_m3_confirmation.py) passes the new parameter, so none of their behavior changes. The already-published v2 confirmation result and its reported metrics remain the authoritative one-shot evidence for the historical M1-M3 chain; this amendment does not authorize or require a new confirmation run.

scope_statement.claim: Fresh-data behavioral confirmation of control discovery, probabilistic identity retention, and calibrated complete-body graph selection
not_claimed: Direct serialization or state handoff from the historical M1 implementation into M2
More than two complete body hypotheses
scope_statement.composition_fact: M2 relearns control relations and M3 extends the M2 entity graph; the historical M1 agent is a stage-specific mechanism check, not a serialized upstream state provider

decision_rule: Authorize design of unprivileged V2-M4 only if every fixed gate passes on the one-shot fresh confirmation. Development results cannot authorize progression, and confirmation failure cannot be repaired by changing this protocol or rerunning its confirmation seeds.
